recent_articles.title: Muslim population in India may match that of Indonesia after Census: Kiren Rijiju - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, Union Minister for Minority Affairs, stated that the Muslim population in India is projected to be nearly equal to Indonesia's population after the upcoming Census. He also expressed concerns over the declining Parsi community and dismissed claims of minority threats, emphasizing equality under the Indian Constitution. **Rijiju** highlighted the BJP's victory in West Bengal as a positive development for national security, citing its border proximity to Bangladesh and concerns about illegal migration.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet approves Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district at a cost of ₹18,133 crore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka** government approved a ₹18,133 crore Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district, which will involve acquiring 7,404 acres of land from nine villages. The Cabinet also gave its approval to the Hyderabad-Bengaluru High Speed Rail Corridor and provided administrative support for the Chennai-Bengaluru high speed rail corridor. Additionally, the government approved a ₹600 crore project for the redevelopment of slums inhabited by minorities across 11 corporations in the state.

recent_articles.title: ‘No one could ever call me anti-women’: Tharoor shares details of conversation with Rijiju - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress MP Shashi Tharoor** and other opposition MPs met with **Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju** after the Lok Sabha adjourned sine die.  **Tharoor** stated that **Rijiju** conceded that no one could ever call him anti-women, highlighting the importance of women's representation in Parliament and institutions. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill to implement 33% reservation for women in legislatures was defeated in the Lok Sabha on Friday after failing to secure a two-thirds majority. The bill proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats to 816 by 2029, following a delimitation exercise based on the 2011 Census.

recent_articles.title: Rijiju writes to Kharge, says delay in women’s quota law will deny justice to millions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, responded to **Mallikarjun Kharge**, Congress President, who criticized the government's push for the Women's Reservation Act implementation.  Rijiju emphasized that the law is about fulfilling promises to Indian women and urged opposition parties to support its implementation in 2029. He stated that delaying action on the matter is unjust and called for a united effort towards "Nari Shakti".

recent_articles.title: Bagalkot bypoll campaign focussed on attacks on individual leaders, leaving out real issues - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The by-elections in **Karnataka** saw a focus on personal attacks rather than addressing key issues like drought and farm labor migration.  **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah**, **Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar**, and **Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil** criticized the BJP candidate, **Viranna Charantimath**, for his perceived arrogance and lack of accessibility to rural voters. **Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal**, a close friend of **Charantimath**, also targeted minority groups and accused him of behaving inappropriately with people.  While both parties engaged in meetings with various caste groups, the campaign was dominated by personal attacks rather than substantive policy discussions.

recent_articles.title: New Rajya Sabha members take oath - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sharad Pawar**, **Ramdas Athawale**, and 17 other new members were sworn in as Rajya Sabha members on Monday, April 6, 2026. The ceremony took place in the Rajya Sabha chamber with **C.P. Radhakrishnan** presiding.  The newly elected members represented various states including Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Odisha.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections: NDA heavyweights set for campaign blitz across State - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Ministers** and national leaders are leading a series of high-profile roadshows and public rallies across Kerala for **BJP-led NDA candidates**.  **Smriti Irani**, **Tejasvi Surya**, and other senior party figures are participating in the campaign blitz, focusing on key constituencies. **J.P. Nadda**, **Kiren Rijiju**, and **Durga Das Uikey** are also actively involved in supporting local candidates. The campaign aims to bolster support for the alliance's regional aspirations.

recent_articles.title: Several minority scholarship schemes discontinued after 2021-22, Minority Affairs Mister tells Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, the **Minority Affairs Minister**, informed the Rajya Sabha that several scholarship schemes for minority students were discontinued after 2021-22.  Payments made in 2022-23 related to pending liabilities, and the government highlighted that these students are still covered under broader schemes like the PM-USP Yojana and the Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The number of beneficiaries declined significantly after 2021-22, with some scholarships merged or limited to specific classes.  **John Brittas**, a CPI-M MP from Kerala, criticized the government's poor utilization of funds allocated for minority welfare.

recent_articles.title: Several minority scholarship schemes discontinued after 2021-22, Minority Affairs Mister tells Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Minority Affairs** has discontinued several scholarship schemes for minority students beyond the 2021-22 academic year.  Responding to a question in Rajya Sabha, **Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju** stated that pre-matric, post-matric, and merit-cum-means scholarships were not approved for continuation after 2021-22. The government highlighted that minority students continue to be covered under broader schemes like the PM-USP Yojana and the Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.  However, data shows a significant decline in beneficiaries and spending on these programs since 2021-22.

recent_articles.title: Government skips FCRA amendment Bill; Rijiju accuses Opposition of spreading ‘wrong things’ before Kerala polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, **Parliamentary Affairs Minister**, announced that the government will not be bringing a Bill to amend the Foreign Contributions (Regulation) Act (FCRA) during the ongoing Budget session.  He accused the Opposition of misleading people in Kerala and across the country regarding the bill, stating it is intended to prevent misuse of foreign contributions and protect national security. **Opposition members**, mainly from Kerala, protested against the provisions of the FCRA (Amendment) Bill, citing concerns about potential restrictions on minority institutions like churches receiving foreign funding.  The protests forced the government to reconsider pushing the bill in the session.

recent_articles.title: Parliament Budget Session LIVE: Lok Sabha adjourned till noon amid Opposition protests over FCRA amendments - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju** announced that the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contributions (Regulation) Act would not be taken up for consideration and passing. **Congress** MPs protested against the bill, accusing the government of attempting to "bulldoze" changes to the FCRA in Parliament. The protests led to the adjournment of the Lok Sabha.

recent_articles.title: 'False, fabricated': Rijiju slams Opposition over claims on FCRA Amendment Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Minister Kiren Rijiju** asserted that the **Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill**, introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25, 2026, aims to regulate foreign funding and prevent misuse of funds for illegal activities. He refuted claims by the Congress and Left parties that it targets religious organizations, stating the bill is intended to protect national security and interests. **Mr. Rijiju** accused these parties of spreading falsehoods to hinder the BJP's support in upcoming Kerala Assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: BJP seeks action against Mamata over ‘MCC breach’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** filed a complaint with the **Election Commission of India (EC)** alleging violations of the Model Code of Conduct by West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. The party accused Ms. Banerjee of making inflammatory statements, inciting violence, and undermining public confidence in the electoral process.  The BJP demanded legal action against Ms. Banerjee, including her debarment from campaigning, enhanced security measures, and increased EC observer deployment.

recent_articles.title: West Asia crisis: Rajnath Singh calls for swift decisions, long-term readiness - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh** chaired the first meeting of the Informal Group of Ministers (IGoM) to monitor the situation in West Asia. The IGoM, which included **Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman**, **Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju**, and other ministers, discussed the impact of the ongoing conflict on India's energy supplies, essential commodities, infrastructure, and supply chains.  **Singh** emphasized a proactive approach to ensure preparedness and safeguard Indian citizens from any potential consequences.

recent_articles.title: Parliament Budget Session LIVE: Rajya Sabha takes up Question Hour - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Lok Sabha** is scheduled to pass the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025 on Friday, March 27, 2026. The proposed amendment aims to expedite IBC cases, facilitate out-of-court resolutions, address cross-border insolvency issues, and streamline discretionary provisions.  The bill passed the Lok Sabha on Wednesday, March 25, 2026, with 32 government amendments. The **Rajya Sabha** will now consider the bill.

recent_articles.title: Parliament will function until April 2; Lok Sabha starts debate on amendments to insolvency & bankruptcy law - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju** announced that the second half of the Budget session would continue as scheduled, with business resuming on Friday (March 27) instead of private members' business. **Mr. Rijiju** also confirmed that Parliament will not function on Saturday or Sunday and will be closed on March 31 for Mahavir Jayanti. The Business Advisory Committee has allocated seven hours of debate for the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026.  **BJP MP Anurag Thakur** highlighted the success of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), citing its impact on debt recovery and changes in debtor-creditor relationships.

recent_articles.title: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju interacts with Bishops and pastors - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kiren Rijiju**, Union Minister of Minority Affairs, met with **Bishops and pastors** from various churches in Tamil Nadu on Saturday. The meeting was organized by the **Tamil Nadu BJP’s Minority Wing**, which included **L. Murugan**, **P. Sudhakar Reddy**, and **J. Johnson**. The event aimed to counter a narrative that the **BJP** is anti-minority, according to party sources.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool MPs walk out of Rajya Sabha protesting removal of officials - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress (TMC)** MPs boycotted the Rajya Sabha on Monday, March 16, 2026, protesting the removal of top bureaucrats by the **Election Commission** ahead of West Bengal Assembly elections.  **Derek O’ Brien**, TMC leader in the House, criticized the decision, while **Kiren Rijiju**, Parliamentary Affairs Minister, condemned the action and accused the party of attacking constitutional bodies. The Election Commission announced the dates for the two-phase election on March 15, 2026.

recent_articles.title: Consensus reached to revoke suspension of eight Opposition MPs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Speaker Om Birla** convened a meeting with floor leaders from both the **government** and **Opposition**, leading to a consensus on revoking the suspensions of eight Opposition MPs. The agreement includes restrictions on disruptive behavior, such as crossing into the Well of the House or protesting at the desk of the secretary general.  The decision comes after seven Congress MPs and one CPI(M) MP were suspended for unruly behavior during the first part of the Budget session.
